decisions.statement: Two functions say the same thing when their shapes match with each bound name read as its order.
A name the function does not bind is read as written unless a name it binds is spelt the same.
A name a destructuring pattern binds is read as its order.
A shorthand name in an object pattern is read as written.
A shorthand name names the property that pattern reads.
Whether the file exports a function is answered beside its rule.
Whether a function only passes names along is answered beside its rule.
A body with a literal or an operator says something of its own.
A body holding no literal and no operator only passes names along.
Whether a body is built only out of literals is answered beside its rule.
A body is built that way where the body answers one literal and does nothing else.
An object or an array is a literal where every key is a name and every value is a literal.
A name held as a value leaves the body built out of more than literals.
A template joining names is no literal however many names that template joins.
A backtick string with no name is a literal as a quoted string is.
A declaration with no body says no rule rather than saying an empty rule.
The source is parsed with parent links.
A body spelling neither `function` nor `=>` is answered without a parse.
A function's export status is answered by climbing to the statement with that function.
Only a function is read.
A rule spelled inline as an expression bound to nothing says no rule here whatsoever.
A name bound to a call answering a function says no rule either.
Only a renaming is defeated, and not one onto a name the code cannot rename.
The same rule written as a loop for a call or with statements reordered reads as another rule.
Nothing here reads the disk or the index.
A rule is the thing the source says.
The use a rule is put to is answered elsewhere.
A parameter's type annotation is a name the function does not bind and is read as written.
A function's type predicate is read as part of that function's rule.
A type predicate is read between the parameters and the body.
The name a type predicate narrows is read as its order.
A return type that is no type predicate is read as nothing.
A type declared on the name a function is bound to is read as nothing.
Two names for one type are two rules here.

definition: what a function does, read so that renaming it or what it binds says nothing new
